messages:
maya_support: FYI support: multiple customers reporting 503s + timeouts hitting hosted /v1/generate around 11:05 UTC. spike shows >30% 5xx on the hosted tier for ~3m. collecting logs now. 

kevin_sre: thanks, can you paste the runner/container logs + node OOM info? suspecting GPU OOM or host OOM leading to SIGKILL. any common model or context size?

maya_support: customers mostly on gpt-medium-open variant, median context ~6k tokens. attaching snippet from one container: 
```
[2026-03-17T11:05:12Z] infer-runner[pid=4321]: ERROR decoder: illegal instruction at 0x7f9a2b1c
[2026-03-17T11:05:12Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4321 (infer-runner) score 123 or sacrifice child
[2026-03-17T11:05:12Z] docker: container exited with status 137
```

kevin_sre: status 137 = SIGKILL from OOM. good catch. are we seeing any host-level memory spike / vmstat? can infra share node metrics?

diana_infra: node pool r8-gpu-2 had a kernel patch yesterday, rolling update completed 02:00 UTC. metric graph shows GPU-mem used spike aligned to 11:05, but also total host memory climbed to 92%. nv-host logs show repeated preemption events on GPU 0.

jhunt_prod: customer impact? which customers and percent of requests failed? we need triage priority P1 if paying customers affected.

maya_support: two midsize customers (prod tenants A & B) hit ~18% of their requests failing during the window. support oncall taking initial CS messages.

kevin_sre: repro plan: try to reproduce with same model + batch size / context on a staging node from same pool. steps: 
1) ssh to a node in r8-gpu-2 pool. 
2) pull image: registry.redwood-infer/internal/infer-runner:2026-03-10-hotfix
3) run load generator: 
```bash
./loadgen --model gpt-medium-open --context 6000 --qps 150 --batch 4
```
collect: dmesg, /var/log/docker.log, nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY every 2s.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: runner image rollback id=sha256:abc123 at 2026-03-10T02:01:02Z (for context)

kevin_sre: mitigation for hosted: enable fallback routing to cpu-quantized variant + throttle burst qps for affected customer routes; set model-swap to smaller-context variant immediately. I'm pushing a routing override to disable r8-gpu-2 for hosting tier while we debug.

jhunt_prod: pls confirm outage window to CS and update SLA hit calc. also want an automated rule: if >10% container exits with 137 in 60s, route to fallback pool.

maya_support: done: informed customers, provided traceback + ETA for mitigation. CS update logged ticket #CS-4572.

kevin_sre: quick findings: reproduced locally with loadgen. root cause appears to be a kernel-level preemption + large KV-cache growth (prefetch) causing host OOM under high context + batch combos. repro steps attached above. next: patch runtime to guard prefetch growth (cap KV prefetch to 1.2GB) and add cgroup memory limit on container to avoid host OOM cascade.

diana_infra: I'll cordon the worst nodes and kick a rolling-recreate overnight if patch verified. also opening infra ticket to revert the kernel patch on r8-gpu-2 if we see correlation.

kevin_sre: follow-up action items: 
- maya_support: collect full docker logs + sample core if possible (if core enabled) -> done?
- maya_support: attach support bundle to #incidents
- kevin_sre: prepare runtime guard PR (cap prefetch), add cgroup mem limit 0.75 * host-free
- diana_infra: cordon nodes + provide metrics export of pre/post changes
- jhunt_prod: confirm customer SLA calc + executive summary

maya_support: support bundle uploaded: link: https://redwood.internal/supp-bundles/CS-4572-3219876543.tar.gz :thumbsup:

kevin_sre: will post PR link and short rollback plan in ~30m. if urgent, set quick revert of kernel rolling update flag.

jhunt_prod: agreed. notify legal/compliance if we need to adjust retention or notify more broadly.

maya_support: closing loop for now, will update when PR merged and nodes stabilized. :white_check_mark:
